_comment: How each Union ministry spends what Parliament voted it, and which ministry each major central scheme sits under. Applied by `npm run db:sync` — see db/README.md.
_sourcing: Every line was read off PRS Legislative Research's Demand for Grants 2025-26 analysis for that ministry and typed in. Each row names the document it came from and links to it. Figures are Rs crore, exactly as the analysis printed them: where it printed a dash the value is null, never zero.
_completeness: Eleven of the thirteen named ministries have an analysis. Chemicals and Fertilisers and Communications have none for 2025-26, so their pages carry the ministry's own series and nothing beneath it. 'Other Ministries' is the source's residual, not a ministry, and has no page at all.
_reconciliation: Checked at authoring time: each ministry's top-level lines were summed and compared against its row in union_ministry_budgets. Eight of eleven agree exactly or to within Rs 1 crore of the source's own rounding. The three that do not are the three whose `basis` says so — Road Transport (Rs 526 crore of recoveries netted off the 2023-24 total), Housing (a selection of schemes, not a partition) and Railways (gross expenditure of Indian Railways, a different and much larger quantity than the Ministry's demand).
_basis: `basis` says what a ministry's lines decompose and whether they add up to its total. It is repeated on every line of a ministry on purpose (migration 009); scripts/lib/stores.js refuses to apply the store if the lines of one ministry disagree about it.
